lesson.sourceStem: A nurse receives report on four patients. Which patient should the nurse assess FIRST? (A) Blood glucose 210 mg/dL scheduled for sliding-scale insulin. (B) Chest pain 8/10 with diaphoresis starting 20 minutes ago. (C) Surgical wound with moderate serous drainage. (D) Mild nausea after morning chemotherapy.

initial.question_stem: Which patient should the nurse assess first?

options.label: A
options.text: A stable patient with glucose 210 mg/dL and scheduled correction insulin

options.label: B
options.text: A patient with new chest pain and sweating

options.label: C
options.text: A stable patient with an unchanged amount of clear wound drainage

options.label: D
options.text: A patient with mild, expected nausea after chemotherapy and no other symptoms

initial.key_cue: The chest pain and sweating are new.
initial.why_correct_short: This combination can signal a heart attack and warrants urgent assessment.

rationales.A: The stated glucose finding needs follow-up, but the scenario describes no acute deterioration.
rationales.C: The drainage is unchanged and the patient is stable; new chest symptoms take priority.
rationales.D: Mild, expected nausea without other symptoms is less urgent than new chest pain and sweating.

initial.one_line_fix: Look for a new, potentially time-sensitive threat among otherwise stable findings.

retry.question_stem: Which patient needs the nurse’s immediate attention?

options.label: A
options.text: A patient with new chest pressure, nausea, and sweating

options.label: B
options.text: A stable patient requesting discharge paperwork

options.label: C
options.text: A patient with unchanged chronic knee pain awaiting routine medication

options.label: D
options.text: A stable patient asking about tomorrow’s appointment

retry.key_cue: New chest pressure occurs with nausea and sweating.
retry.why_correct_short: These symptoms can accompany a heart attack and need urgent assessment.

rationales.B: Paperwork can wait while the nurse assesses new chest symptoms.
rationales.C: Unchanged chronic pain needs care, but the new chest symptoms are more urgent.
rationales.D: An appointment question can wait while the nurse assesses a possible emergency.

retry.one_line_fix: Apply urgency to the whole symptom pattern.
